localChanges: chore: lock the engine packages that let Nuclear units detonate and Settlers clean up pollution

log: A worker cleans the pollution off its tile over the turns the ruleset's MovementCost gives it; finishing processes core-tile-improvement's Removed rules for each Pollution there (civ-clone/web-renderer#32). Registered with registerDelayedAction so a unit part-way through survives a save.

The action processes Moved, then the ruleset's Detonated rules, then destroys the weapon if they haven't (civ-clone/web-renderer#129). SneakNuclearAttack carries the enemy whose peace treaty it breaks, as SneakAttack does.

With Moved first, a ruleset's contact rule met the units about to be destroyed: in civ1-diplomacy that opened a negotiation with a civilization the detonation then wiped out, and the client's patches waited on the answer (found checking civ-clone/web-renderer#129 in the browser).
Each turn, as v474.05 does (CityWorker.cs ~L188-200, L705-768, L3710-3751), for every city (the AI's too, as decided on civ-clone/web-renderer#32):

lib/smokestacks: floor(shields / divisor) + floor(size * level / 4) - 20, where shields are after the Factory/plant bonuses and before unit support, the divisor is the largest PollutionDivisor rule (Hydro or Nuclear Plant 2, Recycling Center 3, else 1) and the level is the polluting advances known (Industrialization, Automobile, Mass Production, Plastics), 0 with Mass Transit.

civ1-city-improvement:city/process-yield/pollution: when 2 * points beats a roll of 0 .. 255 - advances known * difficulty / 2, a random square around the city is polluted, unless it's water, a city or already polluted; emits city:polluted.
PollutionDivisor: a new rule type, so civ1-wonder can add Hoover Dam.
The commented-out Pollution yield modifiers are gone: this replaces them.
test: add simple-world-generator as a devDependency, for the pollution test's FillGenerator
As for a built one, so every player who knows the tile sees its yields change when pollution is cleaned up (civ-clone/web-renderer#32).

A Nuclear unit no longer gets Attack/SneakAttack. It gets NuclearAttack (or SneakNuclearAttack when the target's owner is at peace) against a neighbouring tile holding another player's unit or city, never empty land.
The Detonated rules follow v474.05 (Segment_29f3.cs F0_29f3_0d4d/0ec3):
emit unit:nuclear-detonation before anything changes;
destroy every unit on the target and its 8 neighbours, whoever owns it, except in a city with SDI Defense (emits city:sdi-protected);
halve every city in the area (size -= floor(size / 2)), SDI or not;
pollute each land, non-city tile in the area with a 2 in 3 chance.
civ-clone/web-renderer#129
civ1-unit:unit/action/clean-pollution: a Worker on a polluted square can CleanPollution, which takes 4 turns in Civ1 terms on any terrain (Table 3-2; v474.05 CheckPlayerTurn.cs ~L1050).
Fallout builds the Pollution by constructing it (which processes Built) rather than processing Built a second time, and skips squares already polluted, as v474.05's AddPollutionToCell does.
civ-clone/web-renderer#32, civ-clone/web-renderer#129

Destroying a transport lost at sea destroys its cargo through the Destroyed rules, and the loop over the tile's units then processed that cargo a second time, duplicating unit:destroyed. Skip units already destroyed.
A PollutionDivisor of 2 in its owner's cities on its continent, as a Hydro Plant gives (v474.05 CityWorker.cs ~L741-753, civ-clone/web-renderer#32).
A polluted tile yields half its food, shields and trade, rounded up, after everything else (v474.05 CityWorker.cs ~L4138): a Low priority YieldModifier pushing the difference.
Removed (core-tile-improvement 0.1.6): unregister the improvement, clear the tile's yield cache, emit tile-improvement:removed.
civ-clone/web-renderer#32
For an improvement taken off a tile other than by pillaging, such as pollution cleaned up by Settlers (civ-clone/web-renderer#32).
Re-exported from the new base-unit-action-nuclear-attack package, for Civ1's nuclear detonation (civ-clone/web-renderer#129).
Re-exported from the new base-unit-action-clean-pollution package (civ-clone/web-renderer#32).
